Join us in this role where you’ll carry out specialised inspections, up-tower repairs, troubleshooting and other technical activities across different wind turbine sites and platforms. You’ll combine strong technical capability with a safety-first mindset, sound judgement and the resilience to work effectively while travelling internationally.

Welcome to Special Tasks & Inspections

You’ll be part of the ST&I Travel Technician team, where you and your colleagues will deliver specialist inspections, repairs, technical campaigns and turbine support across Ørsted’s wind turbine sites. As a team, we work in smaller groups across different regions and placing strong emphasis on safety, quality, teamwork and professional development. The role provides exposure to different turbine technologies and complex technical challenges, with opportunities to contribute field experience to improved tools, methods and ways of working.

You’ll play an important role in:

• Conducting turbine condition assessments, end-of-warranty, component and specialist inspections, producing accurate technical reports.

• Perform advanced diagnostic inspections, including endoscopic and stethoscope assessments.

• Carrying out up-tower repairs and support specialised mechanical and electrical activities, troubleshooting complex faults and identifying practical solutions.

• Working within Ørsted's ISO 17020 accredited inspection framework, ensuring compliance, quality and impartiality standards are maintained.

• Leading technical activities as a technical lead, team lead or client representative, collaborating closely with site teams, project teams, OEMs, contractors and technical specialists.

• Contributing to the development and improvement of tools, RAMS, AWPs, work instructions, testing activities and innovative ways of working.

• Championing a strong safety culture, sharing technical expertise, maintaining required competencies and authorisations, and challenging or stopping work where safe execution cannot be assured.

To succeed in the role, you:

• Hold a relevant technical qualification or equivalent hands-on experience, with strong knowledge of wind turbine technology, ideally gained on SGRE or Vestas platforms.

• Apply strong fault-finding and problem-solving skills to unfamiliar and complex technical challenges, developing safe, practical and professional solutions.

• Work independently, prioritising activities and making sound technical decisions when support is not immediately available on site.

• Adapt quickly to different sites, teams and cultures, building effective relationships and representing Ørsted professionally with internal and external stakeholders.

• Communicate clearly in English, producing accurate, structured technical reports and inspection documentation.

• Demonstrate a collaborative, hands-on approach while maintaining the highest standards of safety, quality and professional conduct.

• Be resilient and adaptable, with the ability to undertake extensive international travel and secure the work permits, visas and travel authorisations required for offshore work in the UK, EU, US and Taiwan.

It's an advantage if you also have:

• Experience with endoscopic inspections, turbine condition assessments and component inspections.

• Experience supporting up-tower repairs, major component replacements, technical campaigns and testing activities.

• Relevant OEM authorisations, experience working under Wind Turbine Safety Rules, or within accredited inspection and quality frameworks.

• Strong IT skills, including digital inspection and reporting tools, and additional language capabilities such as German.

The position involves extensive international travel as part of a 14/14 rotation with 12-hour shifts. Assignments may involve unfamiliar sites, teams and working environments. There will also be situations where you are expected to work independently while abroad, while remaining connected to the wider ST&I team. Due to the international nature of the role, candidates must be able to obtain and maintain the necessary work permits, visas and travel documentation required for assignments across the UK, EU, US and Taiwan.

jobs.occupation: Two-year postdoc in developing inventory of agricultural nitrous oxide emissions
jobs.description:
The Department of Environmental Science and the Department of Agroecology at Aarhus University, Denmark, welcomes applications for a postdoctoral researcher position in developing a Tier 3 model-based national inventory of N₂O emissions modelling from cultivation of soils. The position is part of the SmartField project, which is a cross-organizational research project aimed at obtaining knowledge about N₂O emissions from agricultural fields and solutions for mitigation strategies. Additionally, SmartField will develop and deliver an improved methodology for accounting N₂O emissions at farm and national scale.

Expected start date and duration of employment
The position is to be filled by February 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter and is a two-year fixed-term position.

Job description
You will be part of a research environment addressing greenhouse gas emissions and sustainability transition of agricultural systems, with a particular focus on nitrous oxide emissions from agricultural soil aiming to scale emission estimates from the field to the national scale. Your role will primarily involve supporting the development and implementation of a model-based approach for the national of N₂O emissions from diverse agricultural soils, as well as developing the data pipeline. This will include creating and updating spatio-temporal datasets on soils, cropping systems, and field management, and calculating and assessing and comparing the resulting inventories to other approaches. Scenarios will be used to explore how mitigation technologies and management measures could reduce N₂O emissions and to assess the suitability of the proposed Tier 3 modelling framework for Denmark's national N₂O emission inventory. Your work will support a Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) system, enabling transparent, robust and science-based reporting of mitigation progress regarding agricultural field N₂O emission. You will work in close collaboration with colleagues developing and testing process-oriented models, as well as with those responsible for the national greenhouse gas inventory.

Your profile
We are searching for a highly motivated candidate who has:

• A PhD in agronomy, soil science, data science, environmental sciences, engineering, agroecology, biology, or a related field.
• Experience working with models, managing and analyzing large datasets. 
• Experience working with models related to nitrogen/carbon turnover in soil is considered an advantage but is not required.
• Documented experience in scientific writing and publishing in peer-reviewed scientific journals.
• The ability to communicate effectively in English (both written and oral).
• Good collaboration skills and ability to take responsibility to work independently and proactively on the project
Who we are
The position is shared between the Department of Environmental Science and the Department of Agroecology under the Faculty of Technical Sciences at Aarhus University, and it will be hosted by the Land-CRAFT Center at the AU campus in Aarhus.

The Department of Environmental Science is an interdisciplinary department with expertise ranging from physics, chemistry, microbiology, engineering, social science, geography, economics, to policy analysis. Basic as well as applied research are conducted on some of the major challenges facing society, such as pollution and pollution control mechanisms, management of land, soil, water, air and biodiversity, protection of ecosystem services, and climate change. Advisory services within these areas are offered to governmental organizations, non-governmental organizations and companies. The department consists of five sections and currently about 160 staff (including postdocs and Ph.D. students). 

The Department of Agroecology contributes to sustainable solutions to some of the world’s biggest problems within the areas of soil, plants, animals, humans, and the environment. We want to make a difference by contributing to both fundamental knowledge generation and the attainment of sustainable production systems via innovative research, contracted policy advice, and education. We offer professional laboratories, greenhouses, semi-field, and field-scale research facilities, advanced computing capacities as well as an extensive national and international researcher network. The department consists of nine research sections with around 400 highly skilled employees.

This position is hosted by Land-CRAFT - the Center for Landscape Research in Sustainable Agricultural Future, which aims to bring transformational solutions to agricultural systems. Land-CRAFT is a section within the Department of Agroecology. Therefore, there is a strong focus on climate change mitigation and adaptation strategies.

Both departments believe in equality, diversity, inclusion, and creating an attractive work/life balance.

What we offer 
• A collaborative, international research environment that combines high academic standards with an informal and supportive atmosphere. We value accountability, curiosity, flexibility, and teamwork in everything we do.
• An inclusive and respectful workplace culture, where mutual trust, kindness, and professional dialogue are part of daily life. We encourage open communication and develop a cohesive sense of community across teams and disciplines.
• A flexible working environment that supports work-life balance and individual needs.
• An active institutional commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion – in recruitment, career development, and everyday interactions.
• An innovative and meaningful workplace where your work contributes to solving real-world challenges. No two days are alike, and we welcome creative thinking and new ideas.
• Support for international researchers and their families, including Relocation Service and an Expat Partner Programme.
Place of work and area of employment 
The place of work is Aarhus University (LandCRAFT Center), Ole Worms Allé 3, 8000 Aarhus C. The affiliation will be with the Department of Environmental Science. However, it should also be expected that there will be work-related and meeting activities at the Department of Environmental Science which is located at Risø in Roskilde.

Contact information
Further information may be obtained by contacting Head of Section Emissions and Atmospheric Modelling, Professor Peter L. Langen (plangen@envs.au.dk +4520618369), Professor Jørgen E. Olesen (jeo@agro.au.dk +4540821659), or Special consultant related to the national emission inventory Mette Hjorth Mikkelsen (mhm@envs.au.dk +4587158579). 

Deadline
All applications must be received no later than November 27, 2026. 

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

We store summer sun for the winter. Now Photoncycle is heading into thousands of Danish homes, and we are looking for a trainee who wants to help build the market from the ground up. Is that you?

About Photoncycle

Solar panels produce plenty of power in summer and very little in winter, when we need it most. Photoncycle solves that problem: we store the energy in a tank in the ground next to the house, so the household can use it for electricity and heating all winter. Surplus power is sold on the electricity market, where it helps balance supply and demand. The household pays a fixed monthly fee, and we build, install and operate the system.

We are 25 employees with offices in Oslo and Copenhagen. In 2026 we raised a €15 million Series A led by NordicNinja and Voima Ventures. We are now moving from full-scale pilot to commercial rollout, and the first phase of our production plant is underway.

Photoncycle is a completely new technology, and Denmark is our first market.

Why this role

As a trainee, you will be part of building Photoncycle's Danish operations, from research and permit processes to partner dialogues, pilot customers and events. You will work across the full breadth of a market launch and get hands-on experience with how a new energy technology is brought to market in Denmark.

The role is deliberately broad, and the scope will be tailored to the number of hours you work. Tasks will shift as the launch gets closer, and your responsibilities will grow with the role down the line.

What you will do

This is a versatile, hands-on role that mixes research, relationships and the nuts-and-bolts work. You will report to Anne Clara Laugesen, General Manager of Photoncycle Denmark, and work closely with our colleagues in Oslo.

Tasks and responsibility will include:

Market build and operations support

• 
Support our pilot customer programme, from first contact to onboarding

• 
Follow and assist with permit processes and dialogues with municipalities and authorities

• 
Help build and maintain relationships with customers, partners and stakeholders

• 
Take part in preparing test sites and the first installations

Research and analysis

• 
Desk research on municipalities, funding schemes, partners and competitors

• 
Monitor funding and grant opportunities

• 
Collect and structure data and recurring customer questions for internal use

Events and meetings

• 
Practical planning of customer meetings, community events and site visits: invitations, sign-ups, venue, catering and follow-up

• 
Prepare material and logistics for conferences and external events the team attends

What you bring

We imagine you being structured and comfortable juggling many small tasks at once. You take ownership, spot what needs to be done, and ask when something is unclear.

We expect you to:

• 
Be studying, or recently graduated, in a relevant field such as business, energy, engineering, public administration or similar

• 
Write and speak Danish fluently and work comfortably in English

• 
Be confident with Office tools and quick to pick up new systems

• 
Handle confidential information, including customer data, with care

It is a plus if you:

• 
Have an interest in the energy transition, energy systems or the Danish energy market

• 
Have experience from a startup, student job or association work with admin or coordination

• 
Are used to working with AI tools

You don't need to be an energy expert. What matters most is that you enjoy building something new where the right answer isn't known yet – so apply even if you can't tick every box.

What we offer

• 
A front-row seat to building a new energy company in Denmark ahead of a 2027 launch

• 
Close daily collaboration with the GM and real responsibility from day one

• 
Insight into regulation, permits, partnerships and go-to-market in the energy sector

• 
A small, international team with colleagues in Norway

• 
An office in the heart of Copenhagen at BloxHub, with a great lunch setup and free coffee

Start and application

The position can be set up in three ways: as a paid student job (15–37 hours a week), as an internship as part of your studies, or as virksomhedspraktik via your jobcentre if you have recently graduated and are currently unemployed. Hours and tasks are tailored to the arrangement. The start date is yesterday – or whenever you're ready, really.

We will be taking interviews as applications come in.

Photoncycle is committed to an inclusive workplace and hires based on skills, experience and potential. We encourage everyone interested to apply, regardless of gender, age, ethnic background, religion or disability.

We look forward to hearing from you!

SYBO is part of the Miniclip family and known for the widely popular game, Subway Surfers - the most downloaded mobile game in the world, with over four and a half billion downloads. Located in the heart of Copenhagen, we aim to create playful moments that inspire our fans to care.

_Some games chase trends. Subway Surfers helped define an entire genre.

_Now, we're looking for a UI/UX Designer to help shape what comes next.

This is your chance to leave your mark on one of the biggest mobile games ever made. A game with a massive global audience, instant player feedback, and a team that never settles for "good enough". The challenge? Keeping an iconic game feeling fresh, modern, and innovative for hundreds of millions of players around the world.

Come help evolve the visual experience of Subway Surfers, designing new features, game modes, and player journeys while continuously improving the experience that keeps players coming back. Some days you'll be crafting entirely new interfaces. Other days you'll make a tiny change that unlocks a surprisingly big impact. That's the fun part.

If you enjoy solving creative puzzles, have a knack for details, and seeing your work reach millions of players, then this might just be your gig.

**Responsibilities

**

• Actively refine and improve existing UI/UX to elevate player engagement and satisfaction, ensuring Subway Surfers remains intuitive, modern, and enjoyable to play.

• Design and implement intuitive, engaging UI screens, assets, and interactions for new and existing features.

• Create UX wireframes, user flows, and prototypes to support feature development and player experiences.

• Help shape the visual direction of the game's interface, evolving and modernizing the experience, while staying true to the Subway Surfers brand.

• Ensure a consistent visual style, tone, and user experience across all UI elements.

• Create and maintain UI documentation, design systems, and style guides to support consistency and scalability.

• Optimize UI implementations to ensure smooth performance across a wide range of mobile devices.

Life at SYBO

**In your first month...

**You'll get to know the team, the game, and the players that have made Subway Surfers one of the most successful mobile games in the world. You'll be introduced to our tools, workflows, and ways of working while building relationships across the studio. With support from your teammates, you'll begin contributing to your first projects and quickly find your footing as part of the team.

**Within 3 months...

**You'll start taking ownership of more impactful work across the game, designing engaging interfaces and helping improve the player experience through thoughtful UI/UX solutions. You'll collaborate closely with the team to iterate on designs based on player feedback, insights, and performance data.

**By 12 months...

**You'll be a trusted contributor to the future of Subway Surfers, able to lead individual UI/UX initiatives across major features. At this point, your contributions to the UI style guide and visual framework will have enabled a smoother collaboration across teams, ensuring Subway Surfers will remain an evergreen.

**Requirements

**

• A strong portfolio demonstrating solid UI design work for games, with clear examples of creating intuitive, polished, and engaging player experiences.

• Strong ability to create wireframes, user flows, mockups, and polished final designs that effectively balance player needs and business goals.

• Skilled at designing, rendering, and animating high-quality UI elements that bring personality and clarity to the player experience.

• Advanced proficiency with modern UI/UX and prototyping tools, particularly Figma.

• Experience working with Unity and a solid understanding of UI implementation

Bonus Points

• Knowledge of conducting user research and translating player insights into actionable design improvements.

• Experience working on large-scale live service mobile games.

**About SYBO

**We're SYBO, the mobile games studio behind the legendary Subway Surfers, with over 4.5 billion downloads worldwide! Join our team in the heart of Copenhagen, where creativity flourishes in our new, state-of-the-art studio.

If you join us, you'll have the opportunity to dive into exciting and creative projects alongside a diverse group of like-minded colleagues from over 40 countries across the globe.

We truly believe you perform your best, when you have the equipment you need - and our IT team is always on hand to ensure you have access to the latest tools and gear, enabling you to be at your best - even remotely with a home-office budget!

We also pride ourselves in taking care of your well-being, offering a delicious lunch buffet, a variety of healthy snacks, and regular social events to keep the energy flowing.

Not in Copenhagen? Not a problem! We have in-house relocation specialists who will help you relocate, and feel right at home in Copenhagen and at SYBO!

SYBO is committed to providing equal opportunities to all applicants, regardless of race, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.
